guitar.modelsText: Fender Stratocaster / Reverend / Gibson Les Paul
guitar.notes: Accurate: Corgan known for Stratocaster and later Reverend signature; Iha used Les Paul/various.

tone.target: huge mid-scooped fuzz lead with dry alt-rock bite
tone.profile: huge mid-scooped fuzz lead with dry alt-rock bite
tone.summary: Fuzz -> Boost/OD -> Amp (UK 45) -> Cab (UK Vintage 4x12) -> EQ/Modulation. The core sound is built around a Muff-style fuzz into a classic British stack.

blocks.purpose: Clean up pick noise and hum.
Provide the core Big Muff fuzz tone.
Tighten the fuzz and add bite/attack before the amp.
blocks.gap: Using Boost to simulate a mid-hump or tight boost, as no dedicated EQ pre is available for this role.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic Marshall-style British stack.
Provide the classic British cabinet tone.
Achieve the required mid-scooped sound profile.
Add subtle movement and width to the fuzz tone.
blocks.gap: The target is dry/aggressive, so modulation is kept minimal. Chorus adds useful texture without sounding wet.

blocks.purpose: Add minimal rhythmic echo for depth without sounding wet.
blocks.gap: The verdict advises removing delay focus, so settings are kept extremely low to maintain dryness and aggression.

blocks.purpose: Provide a subtle sense of space without muddying the aggressive fuzz.
blocks.gap: The target is dry, so reverb is kept at an extremely low mix to only add dimension.

improvements.summary: Replace the default IR with a more open, mid-scooped cabinet simulation to better match the alt-rock fuzz tone.

proposals.reason: Enhance scooped mids and open sound for aggressive fuzz.
